To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the FhuA-specific host receptor is required for infection by the majority of the phages, and that this is frequently associated with the presence of the cor gene.
a high proportion (85%) of the phages require FhuA for infection, and most of them also carry the cor gene.
a group of heterogeneous mEp lambodid bacteriophages isolated from the feces of different hosts were analyzed to gain insight into their phenotypic traits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the Fhu receptor-dependent phages from the mEp population, which may represent a significant proportion of the phage population in nature.
the analysis of some phenotypically important traits of mEp lambdoids, and it provides evidence of a higher incidence of FhuA-dependent mEp phages and of phages with the cor gene in the environment.
the analysis of phenotypic traits among a group of previously isolated lambdoid phage populations, which may be of interest for the study of phage diversity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
most of the mEp phages are FhuA-dependent, and a significant fraction of them require the λ N antiterminator function.
the majority of mEps from different immunity groups are FhuA-dependent and require the cor gene.
the mEp phage population is heterogeneous and that the majority of the phages are FhuA-dependent and require the N function, but not the λ recombination function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

most FhuA-dependent mEp phages have a similar genome organization to that of the well-characterized phage λ, and they also require the N antitermination factor for their replication, but they differ from phage λ by having a different host receptor for infection.

the majority of phages (37/43; 86%) from different immunity groups require the FhuAp receptor and the cor gene for infection, while a smaller number of phages (6/43; 14%) require the N antiterminator and only two (4.6%) require the λ recombination system.
a large proportion of mEp phage isolates (85%) have evolved to use the FhuA outer membrane receptor for infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the majority of the phages in this group are related to the λ phage and that the FhuA and cor genes are frequently associated in the mEp phages.
the cor gene seems to have a wider distribution than that previously thought.
the FhuA protein and the cor gene are important determinants for the infection of lambdoid bacteriocinogenic phages, which may be relevant for phage therapy.
